chapter_title: Chương 177: Tam Quốc Sát Vượt Biên

segments.title: Chương 177: Tam Quốc Sát Vượt Biên
segments.content:
"CEO Chen, this is Mr. Liu Yumin, Vice President of Chinese Gamer International. CEO Liu is also from Soft-World, the representative they sent to the exhibition this time."

Standing before Chen Guiliang was a man in his thirties.

He was wearing a suit but no tie.

"Mr. Liu, a pleasure to meet you." Chen Guiliang shook his hand enthusiastically.

Liu Yumin smiled and said, "CEO Chen is young and promising. I've long heard of your fame."

Chen Guiliang said, "It is I who have long heard of Mr. Liu's fame. Many boys on the mainland grew up playing 'Tunshi Tiandi'."

Hearing his masterpiece mentioned, Liu Yumin was pleased yet modest, saying, "That game was nothing much. I made it in my university dorm, and it's long been outdated."

"Not at all, a classic is never outdated," Chen Guiliang flattered.

Liu Yumin was even happier for the praise. "'Tunshi Tiandi' is also based on the Three Kingdoms. I personally love the Three Kingdoms. I originally intended to just casually look around at this exhibition in Modu, but I didn't expect to discover your company's 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms'."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Is it Soft-World that wants to be the agent, or Chinese Gamer International?"

Liu Yumin said, "Chinese Gamer International will take the lead to secure the Hong Kong and Taiwan agency rights for 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms'. When operating in Taiwan, we'll certainly make use of many of Soft-World's resources."

"How does Mr. Liu plan to cooperate?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Liu Yumin said, "Chinese Gamer International will take both the online game and the physical card game for 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' in Hong Kong and Taiwan. The total licensing fee will be 250,000 USD. We'll give Game Science a 20% cut for the online game, and a 5% cut for the physical cards."

"Isn't that too little?" Chen Guiliang said.

Liu Yumin explained, "After all, 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' is a card game. The current market in Hong Kong and Taiwan is dominated by MMORPGs."

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "You can't calculate it like that. In the Hong Kong and Taiwan MMORPG market, 'Lineage II' is the sole dominant player. If you were to represent a similar game, you'd be more likely to fail. 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' is perfectly positioned to open up a new track, bypassing 'Lineage II' to attract players. Moreover, cheating software is even more rampant over there than on the mainland. Many games have been killed by cheats. The game mechanics of 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' are naturally designed to avoid a lot of trouble with cheats."

Everything Chen Guiliang said was the honest truth.

If he had created a mainstream online game, it would actually be harder to sell to Hong Kong and Taiwan. "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" was perfectly suited to fill a gap in their markets.

Liu Yumin realized this as well, which was why he was eager to get in touch with Game Science and had even called Soft-World and Chinese Gamer International about it.

If he didn't act fast, by the time the three-day event was over, it was highly likely another agent would snatch it up.

Softstar and Gamania were also here this time, both of them were Liu Yumin's competitors.

Liu Yumin asked, "How does CEO Chen plan to cooperate?"

Chen Guiliang said, "For the 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' online game and physical cards, the total licensing fee for Hong Kong and Taiwan will be 800,000 USD. I want a 30% cut for the online game, and a 15% cut for the physical cards."

"Impossible."

Liu Yumin shook his head repeatedly. "When Taiwanese companies act as agents for mainland online games, the licensing fee has never exceeded 300,000 USD, and the revenue share has never exceeded 25%. For physical cards, the share has never exceeded 12%."

"Mr. Liu, let me remind you. You're asking for the online game plus the physical cards for both Hong Kong and Taiwan, not just the agency for the online game in Taiwan. For a total of 800,000 USD in licensing fees, I'm already giving you a very cheap price," Chen Guiliang said.

Online game agency fees consist of two parts: the licensing fee (upfront payment) and the revenue share.

Part of the licensing fee is paid upon signing the contract, and the full amount must be settled before the game goes live. This is what you often see in the news, when a company spends so many million US dollars to acquire the agency rights for a certain game.

The revenue share is generally paid out on a quarterly basis. Sometimes, a minimum guarantee is required, meaning that even if the game fails and loses money, a minimum monthly fee must still be paid to the developer.

Overseas agencies for physical card games also follow the "licensing fee plus revenue share" model.

Chen Guiliang was only responsible for collecting the money and providing the original art to the Hong Kong and Taiwan agent. The rest of the operations, such as converting to traditional characters, printing, sales, and so on, were entirely handled by the agent.

In this situation, the revenue share for physical cards is very low. For obscure card games, you might only get a 5-8% share.

Liu Yumin wasn't just lowballing; he felt that "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" lacked fame and was offering the lowest market price for Hong Kong and Taiwan.

"Licensing fee of 300,000 USD, 25% share for the online game, 8% share for the physical cards." Liu Yumin raised the price slightly.

Chen Guiliang said, "Why don't we both think it over and talk again another day?"

"Alright." Liu Yumin felt he had been sincere enough. Other agents from Hong Kong and Taiwan wouldn't offer more than him.

As soon as he left, Shin Yoo-bin came in.

After some pleasantries, Shin Yoo-bin gave his offer: for the "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" online game and physical cards in Korea, a licensing fee of 300,000 USD, a 20% share for the online game, and a 5% share for the physical cards.

Chen Guiliang looked at Liang Bin, who was handling the translation. "Are you sure you didn't mistranslate?"

"I'm sure. That's what the Korean said," Liang Bin replied.

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "Too low."

Shin Yoo-bin said, "There are only two companies in Korea willing to represent Chinese games. One is us, and the other is Grigon Entertainment, which represents 'Blade & Sword OL'. Unfortunately, Grigon is poorly managed and is on the verge of bankruptcy. Currently, we are the only ones willing and able to represent 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms'."

Well, well, a monopoly. So cocky.

This was going to be a tough negotiation. They had no competitors.

Chen Guiliang haggled with Shin Yoo-bin for a long time, only managing to increase the licensing fee by 50,000 USD. The online game revenue share was non-negotiable, and the physical card share was raised by 3%.

However, Chen Guiliang was only willing to sign a two-year contract. He would definitely raise the revenue share upon renewal.

Shin Yoo-bin agreed immediately. If "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" succeeded in Korea, it would be a major accomplishment for the company. Renewal would just mean paying a bit more money. If it failed in Korea, then there would be nothing left to say.

The two sides immediately drafted a letter of intent and invited the event organizer over for a very simple signing ceremony.

The actual contract would be signed in a few days, after both parties' legal teams had carefully reviewed it.

The general content of the letter of intent was: Frentic Software company would act as the agent and operator for Game Science's "Legends of the Three Kingdoms OL" and its physical cards. Limited to the Korean region, for a term of two years. Total licensing fee of 350,000 USD, with a 20% revenue share for the online game and an 8% share for the physical cards. A formal contract to be signed within half a month, with the breaching party required to pay a penalty of 30,000 USD.

The junior leader from the organizer who participated in the signing ceremony was very pleased. Every deal facilitated at the exhibition was an achievement for them.

Taiwan's Softstar and Hong Kong's Gamania also came to negotiate one after another.

Their offers were even lower than Liu Yumin's!

Finally, on the third day, Chen Guiliang also signed a letter of intent with Liu Yumin: the Hong Kong and Taiwan agency rights for "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" were packaged and licensed to Chinese Gamer International. The term was for three years. Total licensing fee of 350,000 USD, with a 25% revenue share for the online game and an 8% share for the physical cards.

Whether it was for Hong Kong and Taiwan or for Korea, Chen Guiliang was "selling cheap" this time.

He considered it breaking new ground. He'd deal with it when it came time for renewal.

The employees who had come along were particularly excited. Their game was going international, and they were earning US dollars!

"Why are you circling around me?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Xu Fengyin smiled. "I just want to confirm, will the 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' characters I drew really be seen by players in Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Korea?"

"Yes," Chen Guiliang said.

Xu Fengyin asked again, "What about the Japanese?"

Chen Guiliang said, "No one has approached us yet. Why do you ask about the Japanese?"

Xu Fengyin said, "Most of the comics I read growing up were Japanese. Of course I want my own work to make it to the Japanese market."

"A very practical dream," Chen Guiliang said.

The second day of the event was Public Experience Day.

At nine in the morning, the venue opened, and a flood of gaming enthusiasts poured in.

The booths for The9, Sony, Microsoft, and others were already packed with players. They were here to play "World of Warcraft," as well as PS2 and Xbox console games.

The Game Science booth was deserted.

Xu Fengyin yawned and said, "How come there's no one here?"

Chen Di, who was cosplaying as Cao Cao, said, "Our location isn't great. And most players head straight for the companies they're interested in. If it were me, I'd definitely be running off to play the new PS2 games."

Chen Guiliang didn't join the conversation, leisurely playing "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" with Yang Shuo.

A few minutes later, someone finally shouted, "Quick, come see! There's a Sun Shangxiang and a Zhen Ji over here!"

Four or five young men holding cameras ran over and started snapping pictures of Xu Fengyin and the other female employees.

"Wow, this Zhen Ji is so beautiful!"

"A perfect one-to-one recreation."

"She's not showing enough chest, not at all like in the game."

"Aren't you looking at her face? I think she's even prettier in person than in the game."

Xu Fengyin was proud and shy, subconsciously puffing out her chest and letting the players take photos.

The employee cosplaying as Liu Bei, Zhang Jiabin, couldn't help but complain, "Hey, at least take a picture of the guys too."

"Alright, let's get one of His Majesty too."

"That's so half-hearted. At least try to find a good angle. One more, 'Only with virtue and benevolence can one win over the people.'"

"Why aren't Diaochan and the Qiao sisters here? And what about the newly released Zhurong?"

"We don't have that many female employees."

Someone sat down at the computer next to Chen Guiliang and even greeted him, "I'm an old-school 'LTK' fan. Are you on the Telecom or Netcom server?"

"I play on both," Chen Guiliang said.

The person didn't enter a game room but was looking at the Legend Shows and skins. "Damn, this account is amazing. It's got all the Legend Shows and hero skins. This 'Southern Barbarian Queen' skin for Zhurong is so damn hard to get. I've got enough fragments to craft one."

Chen Guiliang was still quite conscientious.

A few newly released heroes, as well as premium Legend Shows and skins, could only be obtained by opening chests. But there was a safety net of universal fragments, so unlucky players could use fragments to craft them.

Frugal players who really didn't want to spend money could get fragments by logging in daily and completing daily tasks. Over time, without spending a single cent, they could also use fragments to craft heroes, skins, and Legend Shows.

However, for premium skins and premium Legend Shows, the fragments from free play were definitely not enough.

"How many chests did you open?" Chen Guiliang asked.

The person said, "Fifty or sixty."

Chen Guiliang commented, "Then you've got some pretty bad luck."

This guy was so focused on the game, he didn't even take a good look at Chen Guiliang.

In the afternoon was the cosplay competition, with more than 50 participating teams.

The audience below the main stage was packed, just like a concert.

One team after another appeared, drawing continuous gasps from the crowd.

Even though there weren't many onlookers at the "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" booth, there were quite a few fans in the audience. That's because the people with the time and money to attend a game exhibition had a high overlap with the "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" player base.

When Cao Cao, Liu Bei, and Sun Quan led their entourage out, a cheer instantly erupted from the crowd.

Cao Cao took a few steps forward and stopped. A voice line played from the speakers, and many in the audience shouted along, "I would rather betray the world than let the world betray me!"

"Where are the generals of Wei? Someone, guard me!"

"Hahahaha!"

Line after line, whether cringeworthy or domineering, were shouted in unison by the audience along with the speakers.

Many onlookers were baffled by them.

"What game is this? Looks like a lot of people play it."

"I know, it's 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms'. But I've never played it. I didn't know it had so many voice lines."

"I'll download it and try it out later."

A single cosplay show could attract a good number of new users for "Legends of the Three Kingdoms."

Of course, the most sensational group at the event was still the "World of Warcraft" cosplay team.

The whole crowd roared, absolutely insane.

"For the Horde!"

"For the Alliance!"

"Kill the Alliance dogs!"

Chen Guiliang watched with a sigh. In this era, "World of Warcraft" stood alone; nothing else could even compete.

The following events included a CS tournament, a Warcraft III exhibition match, and more. The currently popular player Sky was also invited.

Yang Shuo, on the other hand, was curiously observing everything.

He had graduated from junior high in the countryside, learned auto repair for half a year, and then spent more than three years in the army. He had never dreamed that such an exciting world existed.

After watching a breakdancing show, Yang Shuo took a liking to it.

He thought it was cool.

Everyone was exhausted but had a great time, leaving Modu feeling like they wanted more.

Xu Fengyin returned to Beijing with the team. As soon as she got to the office, a colleague said, "You're famous."

"Huh?"

"Your cosplay photos have gone viral."
